newsitem.title: PERU: Shootout causes alarm near Peru siege site.
newsitem.headline: Shootout causes alarm near Peru siege site.

text.p: A shootout, which at first appeared to be an explosion, within earshot of the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence caused brief panic in Lima on Saturday afternoon.

Witnesses said they heard a loud detonation within a few miles (kilometers) of the residence -- where Marxist rebels are holding 73 hostages -- and local media immediately speculated the noise was a car bomb.
"We heard a very loud boom, and as I looked back I saw birds flying up and away," said Reuters photographer Gregg Newton at the residence.

But police confirmed within minutes that the noise came from a fierce shootout with three criminals, one of whom was injured. "There was an exchange of gunfire ... That was all," one policeman, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.

The roughly 15 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels holding the diplomatic residence have fired into the air at various times during the 32-day hostage crisis to draw attention to their presence.
